name: Ahimoth
title: Levite of the line of Kohath
summary: Ahimot belonged to the Kohathite Levitical branch and appears in the genealogies of 1 Chronicles as a link in the lineage leading to the singer Heman. He was the son of Elkanah and lived in the generations prior to the united kingdom. Heman's family line became especially significant when King David organized the worship service at the sanctuary, and Ahimot's place in this line testifies to his family's long-standing role in Israel's worship life. As a Kohathite, he was part of the Levitical branch traditionally responsible for the holy objects in the tabernacle.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the Levitical genealogy
keyEvents.description: Ahimoth is listed in the genealogy of the Levites in 1 Chronicles, as part of the line of Kohath leading to the singer Heman.

keyEvents.title: Part of Heman's musical lineage
keyEvents.description: Ahimoth belonged to the Levitical line that led to Heman, one of the three chief singers appointed by King David to lead worship at the sanctuary. This lineage highlights the central role of music and praise in Israelite worship.

keyEvents.title: Connection to Elkanah's family
keyEvents.description: Ahimoth was the son of Elkanah and belonged to an extended family line that also touches upon the family of the prophet Samuel. This connection underscores the prominent role of the family in Israel's religious life, although the exact relationship between the various branches is debated.

keyEvents.title: The line of Kohath
keyEvents.description: Through the line of Kohath, Ahimoth's family played a central role among the Levites, as the Kohathites were responsible for the most holy objects in the tabernacle.

versions.summary: Ahimot was a Levite of the Kohathite clan, mentioned in Chronicles as part of the genealogy of the Levites. He was a descendant of Elkanah and an ancestor in the Levitical line of service that served at the tabernacle and later at the temple.
versions.title: Levitical Descendant
versions.reason: [minor] The title 'Levitical descendant' is somewhat generic. A more precise title could link him more clearly to the lineage of Kohath.; [major] Ahimot is not described as a priest in the Bible, but as a Levite in a genealogy. Calling him 'priest' is imprecise; he should instead have the role 'Levite'. Not all Levites were priests – the priesthood was reserved for the descendants of Aaron.; [major] In 1 Chronicles 6, verse numbering varies between different translations. In the Hebrew text (and some translations), Ahimot/Mahot is mentioned in 1 Chron 6:10 (Hebrew numbering) or 6:25 (another numbering). Verse 25 of 1 Chron 6 may match some numberings, but this should be verified. In several translations, the name is given in 1 Chron 6:25 as 'Amasai', while Ahimot is mentioned in verse 25 or 35. The verse number should be checked carefully.; [minor] Verses 31-33 of 1 Chron 6 concern the singers whom David appointed, not specifically Ahimot. The connection is indirect – Ahimot is an ancestor in this line of singing service. The description should make this clearer.; [minor] The child 'Elkana-II' is a reasonable identification, but there are several Elkanas in the genealogy of 1 Chron 6. It must be ensured that this ID actually refers to the correct Elkana – the one who is the son of Ahimot.; [minor] The summary mentions that Ahimot was 'an ancestor in the Levitical service line that served at the tabernacle and later at the temple'. This is reasonable, but it is worth clarifying that his lineage is specifically linked to the singing service organized by David, not necessarily the priestly service.; [minor] Footnotes are missing. Notes should be added about the meaning of the name, the verse numbering issue in 1 Chron 6, and the possible connection with Mahot.

versions.summary: Ahimot was a Levite of the Kohathite clan, mentioned in the genealogy of 1 Chronicles. He was the son of an Elkanah and belonged to the lineage that led to the singer Heman, whom David appointed for the worship service at the sanctuary. Through his place in the Kohathite line, Ahimot was part of a Levitical tradition responsible for service at God's sanctuary.
versions.title: Levite of the line of Kohath
versions.reason: [major] In 1 Chr 6, Ahimoth is mentioned in verse 25 according to the Hebrew numbering, but in many translations this corresponds to verse 10 (or 35). According to the most common numbering in Norwegian translations, Ahimoth appears in 1 Chr 6:10 (Hebrew 6:25). The verse number should be verified – but since the profile already notes numbering variations in the footnotes, one consistent numbering system should be chosen and followed throughout.; [minor] The phrasing "the same extended lineage as the prophet Samuel" may be imprecise. Ahimoth belongs to Heman's lineage, which indeed overlaps with Samuel's line in 1 Chr 6, but the exact relationship between Ahimoth and Samuel is debated. It would be better to phrase this more cautiously.; [minor] The child is listed as "elkana-ii". In 1 Chr 6:25–26 (Hebrew numbering), Elkana follows Ahimoth in the lineage, but the ID "elkana-ii" should be verified against the actual ID used in the database for this Elkana.; [minor] The summary closely resembles version 1 in the introduction ("Ahimoth was a Levite from the family of Kohath, mentioned in the genealogy..."). It should be rephrased more distinctly to set it apart from the earlier version.; [minor] Verses 31–33 refer to Heman's appointment as a singer, not directly to Ahimoth. This is contextually relevant but should clearly be marked as background information rather than a direct reference to Ahimoth.

footnotes.text: The name Ahimot (אֲחִימוֹת) is composed of the Hebrew roots אָח (akh, 'brother') and מוֹת (mot, 'death'), and can be translated as 'my brother is dead' or 'brother to death.' Such names may reflect a family's grief at birth, a practice known from several Semitic cultures.

The verse numbering in 1 Chronicles chapter 6 varies between the Hebrew Masoretic text and translations based on the Septuagint. Ahimot can be found in verse 25 (Hebrew) or verses 10/35 in other traditions. This is because the chapter is organized differently in various textual traditions.

Some textual critics identify Ahimot with the name 'Mahat' (מַחַת), which appears in 1 Chron 6:20, suggesting it may be a scribal variation. Other scholars keep them separate as two different persons, since the genealogies in which they appear are distinct.

According to Num 4, the Kohathites had a special responsibility for the most holy items in the tabernacle, including the ark of the covenant, the table of showbread, the seven-branched lampstand, and the altars. Ahimot's belonging to this clan places him within this priestly tradition.

The lineage that includes Ahimot leads in 1 Chron 6 to the singer Heman, one of three chief singers whom King David appointed for the worship service at the sanctuary. Heman's genealogy is traced back through the Kohathites all the way to Levi, legitimizing the musical-liturgical function as an inherited Levitical service.

The relationship between the various persons named Elkanah in 1 Chron 6 is debated in scholarship. The genealogy mentions several men with this name in the line of Kohath, and it is unclear whether they are different individuals or if some names are repetitions due to textual transmission. Both Ahimot's father and son bear the name Elkanah, which may indicate a naming tradition within the family.
